name: Caldero Workheat Thermal
description:
A heavyweight thermal undershirt from Caldero Industrial, the kind that's been the standard-issue underlayer for dock workers and warehouse crews across the Lakes corridor for forty years. Waffle-knit synth-cotton in faded brick red or charcoal grey, with flat-felled seams that won't dig into skin under a harness or safety vest. The collar is a low crew that doesn't bunch under a jacket. Reinforced at the elbows and the lower back where workers bend and strain. It smells faintly of the industrial washing process when new, and after a few cycles it softens into something almost pleasant.

Caldero doesn't market this shirt. It doesn't need to. It shows up in every supply locker in every cold-floor facility from the Gray Zone level to the mid-stacks. Tier 2 workers buy it three at a time. Tier 1 residents find it secondhand, cut the sleeves off, patch the holes. It's the kind of garment that outlives its owner's job.
what_it_says: You work with your body. You're not trying to impress anyone. You showed up.
worn_by: the Gray Zone residents in secondhand condition
anyone who gets cold on the job
story_hooks: A Caldero thermal with a specific batch code from 2197 was the only thing linking three bodies found in the sub-level drains — they all worked the same ghost shift at a facility that officially doesn't exist.
A Tier 4 fashion house released a 'distressed heritage' version for Φ380. The backlash from actual workers who wear the real thing turned ugly fast.
Someone has been leaving Caldero thermals — clean, folded, with a single Quanta coin tucked inside — on doorsteps of laid-off workers in Stack 7. Nobody knows who.

physical_description.visual_profile: A utilitarian base layer with honest, unpretentious construction. The waffle-knit texture reads as lived-in and durable rather than fashionable. On the body, it creates a clean, fitted silhouette that disappears under outer layers but holds its own if worn alone—the kind of shirt that looks better after a season of use than it does fresh from the warehouse.
physical_description.fit: Fitted but not tailored. Straight through the torso with enough room for layering under harnesses and tactical gear. Sleeves hit mid-forearm with a subtle taper. The low crew neck sits flat against the collarbone, designed to be invisible under jackets and safety equipment.
physical_description.primary_material: Waffle-knit synth-cotton blend—a practical hybrid that breathes while maintaining thermal properties. The synthetic component ensures it survives hundreds of industrial laundry cycles without degrading.
physical_description.texture: Waffle knit creates micro-dimensional surface with subtle tactile variation. Fabric is dense and slightly napped, with a soft hand once broken in. Flat-felled seams are the signature detail—visible topstitching that runs flat against the skin, no raw edges to catch or irritate.
physical_description.color_scheme: Faded brick red or charcoal grey—industrial colorways chosen for practicality (hides stains, doesn't show wear patterns). Both shades have a matte, slightly desaturated quality suggesting decades of laundry cycles.
physical_description.closures: None. Simple pullover construction with no fasteners—speed and simplicity for workers getting dressed in cold corridors.
distinctive_features: Flat-felled seams throughout—visible topstitching, ergonomic construction for harness wear
Reinforced elbow patches in slightly heavier knit
Reinforced lower back panel for bending strain
Low crew neck that won't bunch under jackets
Subtle Caldero woven label at side seam—understated, no branding theater
Fading patterns that develop from use, not design intent
physical_description.tier_indicator: Tier 3 functional. Standard-issue working class. Tier 2 buys new; Tier 1 and Tier 5 find it secondhand and repurpose it.
physical_description.cultural_context: This is dock worker, warehouse crew, maintenance tech gear. Wearing it new signals honest labor. Wearing it worn and patched signals street credibility or long-term subcultural involvement. In high-tier contexts, it's worn ironically or deconstructed as vintage.
physical_description.condition_typical: Breaks in beautifully. Fresh examples look stiff and slightly plasticky. Worn examples have softened fabric, minor pilling in high-friction zones, possibly patched elbows. Smell becomes neutral or faintly mineral after breaking in. Some examples show bleach spots or oil stains that survived dozens of washes.
